extracted.intended_audience: naturalists, anatomists, and early-modern natural philosophers (readers of Philosophical Transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing a systematic anatomical account of a dissected specimen: record provenance, external and internal morphology, measurements, comparisons to other authors/species, and functional interpretations, illustrated by figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: State specimen provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: This which we dissected was sent to Mr. Henry Loades ... from Virginia; who was pleased not only to gratify the curiosity of the Royal Society in showing it alive, but likewise gave it them when dead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report where the specimen came from, who provided it, whether it was shown alive or received dead, and any relevant collection/context details so readers can judge representativeness and trace the material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare specimen count and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The observations I shall here give are such as a single subject would afford, not what might complete the history of so curious an animal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state if the account is based on a single specimen (or few) and the resulting limitations; distinguish between observations that a single subject supports and those requiring repeated dissections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify scope of the report
rubrics_metrics.description: But I shall concern myself at present only with the anatomy, which I think is yet given by none;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare which aspects (e.g., anatomy, behaviour, distribution) are being treated and which are deferred, so readers understand the intended coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite and compare prior literature
rubrics_metrics.description: For other accounts I shall refer to Marcgravius, Piso, Johnston, Nierembergius, De Laet, Hernandez, and others who have written of it;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference earlier authors, compare existing accounts with current observations, and note agreements and disagreements with evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe external morphology first
rubrics_metrics.description: Before we look within, we shall take a short survey of its outward parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a systematic external description (shape, head, scales, coloration, counts) before internal anatomy, to give readers an orienting overview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide quantitative measurements and counts
rubrics_metrics.description: This that we dissected was 4 feet 5 inches long; the girt of the body ... was 6½ inches; ... From the neck to the anus we numbered 168; beyond the anus were two half scales ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record precise measurements (lengths, girths, diameters) and counts (scales, vertebrae, chambers) wherever possible to make descriptions reproducible and comparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include high-quality figures and refer to them constantly
rubrics_metrics.description: I shall therefore in my description, the better to help out and illustrate my meaning, have a constant reference to the figures; which, being anxious to make as well as might be, I spent so much time...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide labeled illustrations referenced in the text; invest effort in accurate plates/figures so visual evidence complements verbal description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe structural relationships and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: The scales of the belly were joined to each other by distinct muscles; the lower tendon of each muscle being inserted into the upper edge of the following scale ... To each scale was appropriated a rib, whose point joined with the extreme of it...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how parts are connected (muscles, tendons, ribs) and how these attachments relate to function (e.g., locomotion), not merely list parts in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infer function from structure, with comparative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: These muscles ... must much advantage the use nature seems to design them for, by strengthening them to perform their reptile motions; ... Whence it is observed by Nierembergius, that on rocks their motion is much quicker than on the earth or plains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer hypotheses about the function of anatomical features, support them with observations and comparisons to related species or environments, and indicate when conjectural.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record internal anatomy and its subdivisions with roles
rubrics_metrics.description: So that the whole ductus alimentalis, from its uses, may ordinarily be divided into 4 parts. 1. That which conveys the food, the oesophagus. 2. That which digests or corrodes it, the stomach. 3. That which distributes the chyle, the intestines, 4. That which empties the faeces, the rectum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize internal systems into functional subdivisions and describe the morphology and presumed role of each part for clarity and comparative purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note preservation and handling constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: I spent so much time, that I had not an opportunity of satisfying my curiosity in all respects (the parts drying) as I desired;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record any preservation issues (drying, decomposition) that limited observations; where feasible, take steps to prevent drying so delicate structures can be examined fully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish observation from conjecture
rubrics_metrics.description: For the tortoise ... it is not unlikely for this reason; that it might not be forced so often to raise itself out of the water to breathe ... So perhaps that of air too, a more constantly requisite supply of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing physiological explanations, label them as conjectural and support with comparative or experimental evidence where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and correct previous misdescriptions with evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Charas is much mistaken, who supposes them to be the parastatae or conservatories of the seed ... and I the more wonder at this his mistake, since he could not but have observed them, as I have, in the female vipers too; which sufficiently shows his error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically evaluate earlier accounts; point out specific errors and provide empirical counter-evidence (e.g., observing same structures in females) to justify corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record sexual dimorphism and anatomical variation
rubrics_metrics.description: The two testes ... the right being 2½ inches long, the left but 1½ inch long ... I shall add, that the ovarium of the female viper is the same; for that of one side was as big again as the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note asymmetries, size differences between left/right and between sexes, and consider their implications for function and classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose names and consistent terminology while justifying them
rubrics_metrics.description: I have taken the liberty of placing it in that class, and (since it has not yet, that I know of, any Latin name) of giving it that of vipera caudisona; ... I shall therefore call them retractores penum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce consistent terms or names for newly observed structures or taxa, and justify choices (morphology, provenance); make clear when names are authorial proposals versus established terms.
